correctness.rationale: The signed paperfolding prefix height is exactly the Gray-code Hamming weight \(H(N)=s_2(N\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}\lfloor N/2\rfloor)\), since the symbol at \(N\) is the sign of its Gray-code weight change. The reflected-block identity \(\mathcal H_m=\mathcal H_{m-1}\Vert(1+\operatorname{rev}\mathcal H_{m-1})\) forces every midpoint-crossing Dyck interval to run from \(2^r-1\) to \(2^m-1\); noncrossing intervals inherit the property inductively. For fixed \(L=2^K-2^r\), later reflection interchanges exactly the two possible offset residues \(2^r-1\) and \(2^K\) modulo \(2^{K+1}\), and creates no new midpoint-crossing interval of length \(L\). Both residue classes are genuine Dyck starts: their factor positions have \(2\)-adic valuation less than \(K\), so shifting by \(2^{K+1}\) preserves every symbol. A designated symbol distinguishes the two canonical words except at lengths \(2\) and \(4\), and exact residue counting yields natural density \(2^{-K}\) and the dyadic-prefix occurrence formula. Exhaustive independent computations check all intervals through depth \(12\) and prefix-height equality through \(2^{18}\).

value.rationale: The original work explicitly asks about Dyck factors in paperfolding. The theorem does more than give a sparse list of admissible lengths: it completely classifies occurrence positions as two residue classes modulo an explicit power of two, decides each candidate occurrence by a single modular test, gives exact natural occurrence density, and determines the number of distinct Dyck words at every length. This is a natural full positional classification of a classical automatic sequence and closes a separate multiplicity gap beyond the known length-support phenomenon.
